skill.name: network-engineering
skill.description: Guide for network architecture, DNS, TLS, load balancing, and connectivity troubleshooting across cloud and traditional environments.
skill.summary: Design network topologies, debug connectivity, and review DNS, TLS, and load balancer behavior.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: No malicious intent, prompt injection, credential access, or automatic execution was found. The static findings are documentation artifacts: Markdown formatting, reserved or private IP examples, and standard network diagnostic commands for authorized troubleshooting.

remediation.issue: Network diagnostic commands lack an explicit authorization boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that probes, traces, scans, and packet captures must only target systems the user owns or is authorized to test.

remediation.issue: Example commands can be copied directly into live environments.
remediation.suggestion: Label commands as examples and remind users to review targets, ports, and impact before execution.

remediation.issue: One DNS example uses a public resolver address.
remediation.suggestion: Explain when to use public resolvers versus internal resolvers during troubleshooting.

content.value_statement: Complex networks fail in many layers, so troubleshooting can become slow and inconsistent. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured references for design, DNS, TLS, and connectivity analysis.
actual_capabilities: Maps OSI layers to protocols and troubleshooting tools.
Suggests VPC subnet layout patterns for public, private, and database tiers.
Compares load balancer types and routing strategies.
Explains DNS record types, TTL choices, and propagation checks.
Guides TLS certificate and cipher configuration reviews.
Provides checklists for connectivity, performance, MTU, and packet capture diagnostics.
limitations: Does not run commands or change infrastructure by itself.
Uses generic examples that must be adapted to real environments.
Does not replace vendor documentation or change approval processes.
Requires authorization before active probing, packet capture, or production testing.

use_cases.title: Plan cloud network layout
use_cases.description: Design public, private, and database subnet tiers with clear traffic flow and routing assumptions.

use_cases.title: Diagnose service connectivity
use_cases.description: Work through DNS, routing, firewall, port, and application checks during an outage or deployment issue.

use_cases.title: Review DNS and TLS readiness
use_cases.description: Check record strategy, certificate coverage, TLS versions, and safe migration timing before a launch.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Network Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain a safe VPC subnet design for a three-tier web application. Include public, private, and database tiers with traffic flow.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Connectivity
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me diagnose why an application cannot reach its database. Ask for missing details, then organize checks by DNS, routing, firewall, and service state.

prompt_templates.title: Review DNS and TLS
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned DNS and TLS setup for a production launch. Identify record, TTL, certificate, and rollback risks.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Incident Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a network outage runbook for authorized operators. Include triage order, decision points, evidence to collect, escalation criteria, and safe rollback steps.

output_examples.input: A user asks why a web service is intermittently unreachable.
output_examples.output: The skill would produce a layered checklist that separates DNS, routing, firewall, load balancer, and application causes.

output_examples.input: A platform team needs a load balancer decision.
output_examples.output: The skill would compare application, network, classic, and gateway load balancers against protocol, routing, and performance needs.

output_examples.input: A security team prepares a DNS and TLS review.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline record validation, TTL planning, certificate coverage, TLS version policy, and rollback concerns.

best_practices: Confirm ownership and authorization before any probe, trace, scan, or packet capture.
Start with DNS, routing, firewall, and application checks before changing infrastructure.
Document expected traffic flows, ports, TTL values, and rollback steps before production changes.
anti_patterns: Running diagnostic commands against third-party systems without explicit authorization.
Treating sample CIDR blocks, domains, or ports as production-ready values.
Changing load balancer, DNS, or firewall settings before collecting baseline evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill execute network commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples; the user or agent must decide and authorize any execution.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only for cloud networks?
faq.answer: No. It includes cloud-oriented VPC examples and general DNS, TLS, routing, and connectivity guidance.

faq.question: Does it cover network security?
faq.answer: It covers security-related basics such as TLS, subnet isolation, DNS controls, and safe troubleshooting boundaries.

faq.question: Can it replace vendor documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a planning and troubleshooting aid alongside platform documentation and internal change procedures.

faq.question: How should packet capture be handled?
faq.answer: Use packet capture only with authorization, defined scope, retention limits, and care for sensitive payload data.
